standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that invertibility modulo a square-zero ideal implies invertibility, via the inverse image description of the units.

core_obligations: Unwrap the definition: for an ideal I of square zero in a ring A and a map from R to A whose composite with A to A/I inverts every element of S, one must show it already inverts them (proof lines 41465-41468).
Use that the units of A are exactly the inverse image of the units of A/I under the canonical map, which settles the lifting condition (proof lines 41468-41470).
proof_roadmap: Translate formal etaleness into the concrete lifting condition on inverting elements of S (proof lines 41464-41468).
Apply the inverse-image description of the units to discharge it (proof lines 41468-41471).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for any multiplicative subset S of a ring R the localisation map from R to S^{-1}R is formally etale (statement lines 41458-41462). The proof does not invoke the standard equivalent formulations from the literature: it unwraps the infinitesimal lifting condition into the concrete statement that a ring map into A which inverts the elements of S modulo a square-zero ideal I already inverts them in A, and then uses that the units of A are the inverse image of the units of A/I (proof lines 41464-41471). Choosing the right unwrapping and the inverse-image description of the units is the content. H2.
